children: stock jumped 2.3% in early Friday trading after Roth upgraded the bond insurer to Buy due to limited impact from a Florida railroad's Chapter 11 bankruptcy and an increased likelihood of the company resuming stock buybacks.
Brightline Florida Holdings, a high-speed railroad from Miami to Orlando, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy
some of its debt. However, the bankruptcy filing didn't include Brightline Trains Florida LLC, the obligor to tax-exempt senior bonds insured by Assured Guaranty
Under the restructuring Brightline's new operating company will receive $490M of new capital. Assured Guaranty

has committed to invest $70M in the new pari passu senior debt. It had also provided bond insurance on $1.133B of its senior debt, which will now total $1.203B, a note from Roth analyst Harry Fong explained.

will resume its share repurchase program, which had been suspended since 2013, once the court approves Brightline's restructuring. "With hindsight, we believe concerns over Brightline were chiefly behind the suspension," Fong wrote. "We would not be surprised if the 'new' repurchase program were less than $500M a year going forward, as the company is now looking to grow its life annuity business that will need more capital."
